James Exon]] | after_party = Democratic Party (United States) }} {{Elections in Nebraska}} The '''1990 United States Senate election in Nebraska''' was held on November 5, 1990. Incumbent Senator [[J. James Exon]] ran for re-election to a third term.{{cite news|last=Heussmann|first=Annette|title=Exon announces bid for third Senate term|newspaper=[[Star-Herald]]|date=February 6, 1990|location=[[Scottsbluff, Nebraska]]|page=2|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/star-herald/190876457/|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|access-date=February 8, 2026}} He was challenged by Republican nominee [[Hal Daub]], who had previously represented the [[Nebraska's 2nd congressional district|2nd congressional district]] before unsuccessfully running for the U.S. Senate in [[1988 United States Senate election in Nebraska|1988]]. National Republicans targeted Exon's seat, given President [[George H. W. Bush|George Bush]]'s landslide victory in the state in [[1988 United States presidential election in Nebraska|1988]] and Exon's narrow victory in [[1984 United States Senate election in Nebraska|1984]].{{cite news|title=Atwater says state among the most promising for GOP|newspaper=[[Grand Island Independent]]|date=February 9, 1990|location=|page=3|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-grand-island-independent/190875732/|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|access-date=February 8, 2026}} However, the [[1990 United States elections|midterm elections]] saw comparatively little change nationwide, and saw the fewest number of Senate seat changes since the ratification of the [[Seventeenth Amendment to the United States Constitution|Seventeenth Amendment]] in 1913. Exon ultimately defeated Daub in a landslide, winning 59% of the vote. This was the last time that a Democratic candidate won the Class II Senate seat in Nebraska, and Exon remains the only Democrat to have held this seat in the Senate. == Background == In [[1984 United States Senate election in Nebraska|1984]], despite [[Ronald Reagan]]'s [[1984 United States presidential election|landslide presidential victory]] in the concurrent election,{{Cite news |last=Raines|first=Howell|date=November 7, 1984|title=Reagan Wins By a Landslide, Sweeping at Least 48 States; G.O.P. Gains Strength in House|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1984/11/07/politics/reagan-wins-by-a-landslide-sweeping-at-least-48-states-gop-gains.html|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170825144938/http://www.nytimes.com/1984/11/07/politics/07REAG.html?pagewanted=1|archive-date=August 25, 2017|access-date=March 12, 2025|work=[[The New York Times]]|language=en-US|issn=0362-4331}} J. James Exon held the Senate seat, defeating Republican Nancy Hoch with nearly 52% of the vote. By contrast, Reagan won Nebraska in the presidential election with 70% of the vote to 28% for Democratic candidate [[Walter Mondale]].{{Cite web |last=Ladd |first=Thomas E. |date=May 1, 1985 |title=Statistics of the Presidential and Congressional election of November 6, 1984 |url=https://clerk.house.gov/member_info/electionInfo/1984election.pdf |access-date=July 2, 2025 |website=[[Clerk of the United States House of Representatives|Clerk of the House of Representatives]] |page=33}} == Primaries == === Democratic primary === ==== Candidates ==== * [[J. County]] Attorney{{cite news|title=Staskiewicz seeks 2nd District seat|newspaper=[[York News-Times]]|date=March 1, 1990|location=|page=5|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/york-news-times/190877351/|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|access-date=February 8, 2026}} ===== Campaign ===== Congressman [[Doug Bereuter]], who was passed over for an appointment to the U.S. Senate in 1987, considered running for the Senate against Exon, and was heavily recruited by national Republicans.{{cite news|last=Lynch|first=David E.|title=Bereuter must make a difficult decision|newspaper=North Platte Telegraph|date=April 16, 1989|location=|page=4|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/telegraph/190876888/|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|access-date=February 8, 2026}} However, on June 5, 1989, Bereuter announced that he would not seek the Republican nomination, and would instead seek [[1990 United States House of Representatives elections in Nebraska#District 1|re-election]], citing a lack of "adequate campaign resources" for a statewide campaign with a competitive [[1990 Nebraska gubernatorial election|gubernatorial election]] and the possibility that Republicans would lose his seat. Following Bereuter's decision to not challenge Exon, former Congressman [[Hal Daub]] emerged as the favorite candidate of national and state party leaders. [[Douglas County, Nebraska|Douglas County]] Attorney Ron Staskiewicz explored a campaign, and launched a statewide tour in anticipation of a possible campaign.{{cite news|title=Staskiewicz to launch 8-day whistle-stop tour across state|newspaper=[[Lincoln Journal-Star]]|date=December 24, 1989|location=|page=4D|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/lincoln-journal-star/190877478/|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|access-date=February 8, 2026}} Daub announced his campaign on February 12, 1990, and Staskiewicz announced shortly thereafter that he would [[1990 United States House of Representatives elections in Nebraska#District 2|run for Congress]] from the [[Nebraska's 2nd congressional district|2nd district]]. Daub's only challenger in the Republican primary was Otis Glebe, a real-estate investor.
